title: Early saxophone players: Tio, Dutrey, John and Willie Joseph
summary: They try to name the first New Orleans saxophonists and discuss Willie Joseph and Bab Frank.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Yeah, I forgot to tell you hello from below, Bonds. Remember the saxophone player which I left there? I met him on the street and he said to be sure and tell you hello. Oh, tell him the same for me. I will. I wanted to ask you about saxophone there. You remember him, huh? Yeah. Mealy Barnes, his little brother? His little brother, Mealy's little brother. But anyway, who was the first one to play a saxophone in New Orleans that you heard then?
Hmm. Oh, it's hard to say all now because it looked like when one picked it up the whole bunch started playing. Yeah.
All of a sudden. Well who started the fast thing right on the saxophones?

Because you take a fellow like Louis, he never did play nothing but that clarinet. No, he wasn't. But you take Tio, Tio had a saxophone, take Sam Dutrae, this fellow there, he had a saxophone. And who else? Two or three.
John Joseph had one early, huh? You remember that?
Oh yeah, John Joseph. I remember the Joseph.
He's still playing. He's only 85. Huh? No, he's still. 86. He's still here. He still plays bass in New Orleans. Oh, I see. Cuts hair by day and plays bass at night. Wasn't he a president?
No, and Willie Joseph. Where is he at? He's the one that should be playing that saxophone.
He passed. He passed. He passed. He was hit by a car, hit one driver. Came back from California to visit his brothers and got one of them. He was a pastor. Palleter you're talking about.
Willie I used to call him. He played with us too already. But he didn't play saxophone then, he was playing clarinet. With who? Which band? With the Silver Leaf band. There's a band right there.
Oh yeah. Did he play before Dutri?

But no. Substitute. Substitute, that's right. For instance, Dupre couldn't play, you see. Whenever he couldn't play with this fellow, we hired anybody who we couldn't get. That's the way, that's how I come to play with some of that fellow you were talking about playing that piccolo.
Bad Frank, yeah. That was his name, Bad Frank. I remember that.
